study_design: Two population-based case-control interview studies, one in Black men and one in White men, each with age-matched population controls.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Both studies included 142 pairs of cases and population controls matched on age.
reason: The abstract evaluates risk factors for prostate cancer in two case-control studies but does not analyze an aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, high-risk, or lethal incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: While beta-carotene was not consistently related to risk, there was some indication that in persons with low fat intake, low beta-carotene intake may be associated with high risk.
estimate_classifications.reason: This row concerns beta-carotene and overall prostate cancer risk; no aggressive disease definition is given.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Fat intake was a risk factor for prostate cancer in both populations, but vitamin A consumption and protein intake were inconsistently related or unrelated to prostate cancer risk.
estimate_classifications.reason: The vitamin A association is explicitly with prostate cancer generally, not an aggressive subtype.
